title: Seller Property Condition Disclosure Statement
description: Nebraska requires sellers of residential real property to complete and deliver a Seller Property Condition Disclosure Statement to the buyer before acceptance of an offer. The statement covers structural, mechanical, environmental, and other known material conditions. Exemptions include transfers by court order, foreclosure, and transfers between co-owners.

required_actions.note: Must be delivered before acceptance of an offer to purchase. Buyer may rescind within 3 days of receipt if not provided timely.

title: Agency Relationship Disclosure
description: Nebraska licensees must provide a written agency disclosure to all parties at the first substantive contact. The disclosure must explain the types of agency relationships available (seller's agent, buyer's agent, dual agent, designated agent, subagent). Dual agency requires written informed consent from both parties.

title: Closing Type — Title Company / Escrow
description: Nebraska residential real estate closings are typically handled by title companies or escrow agents. Attorney involvement is not required by statute but is recommended. Title insurance is customary and typically paid by the seller.

required_actions.note: Title company or escrow agent conducts closing. Attorney optional but recommended.

title: Lead-Based Paint Disclosure (Pre-1978)
description: For residential properties built before 1978, sellers must provide the EPA-mandated lead-based paint disclosure, the EPA pamphlet 'Protect Your Family From Lead in Your Home,' and allow a 10-day inspection period. This is a federal requirement enforced at the state level.

required_actions.note: Buyer has 10-day inspection opportunity unless waived in writing.

title: Radon Awareness Disclosure
description: Nebraska has among the highest radon levels in the U.S. While not a statutory mandate for seller disclosure, the Nebraska Department of Health and Human Services strongly recommends radon testing and disclosure. The seller property condition disclosure form includes a radon question. EPA Zone 1 designation covers most of the state.

required_actions.note: Radon section on NE-SPCDS. Recommend buyer obtain independent radon test.
